nodes.label: Pregnant patient presented with sudden massive blood loss, hemoptysis, and dyspnea
Patient is a 29-year-old pregnant Chinese woman at 29 weeks of gestation with no significant past medical history.
Blood loss suddenly reached 500 ml within half an hour, and the patient entered the emergency room with hemoptysis and dyspnea.

Physical examination showed temperature 37.2°C, pulse rate 101 beats/min, respiratory rate 20 breaths/min, blood pressure 90/60 mmHg, and chest examination revealed few moist rales and dry crackles in both lungs.
Hemoglobin is 81 g/L, confirming significant blood loss
Platelet count and coagulation function are normal
Bronchial artery CTA shows tortuous thickened bronchial arteries and right lung increased density
Obstetric hemorrhage due to placental abruption with pulmonary hemorrhage
Obstetric hemorrhage due to placenta previa with pulmonary hemorrhage
Obstetric hemorrhage due to uterine rupture with pulmonary hemorrhage
Obstetric hemorrhage with pulmonary hemorrhage from bronchial artery lesion
